CallBackery 0.61.3 - BENIGN

Target SHA256:
1982bb548e20a5f83a586bdfda3ee7a61374f6b62462642980a248a14bbab56b

Purpose and execution paths
CallBackery is a Perl Mojolicious/Qooxdoo CRUD web application framework.
t/doc-traversal.t writes POD containing a canary to a temporary directory,
constructs a double-colon traversal, and sends it through Test::Mojo against
its own app. Assertions require rejection and absence of the canary. The
production Doc.pm route converts slashes to module separators, checks the
entire name against \A\w+(?:::\w+)*\z, and returns 404 before lookup on failure.
The permitted path is opened with three arguments and rendered as POD.
The traversal literal is accurate notable evidence, not a demonstrated
unauthorized access. No filename-based or product-name exclusion was added.

Release evidence
Fetched from https://cpan.metacpan.org/authors/id/O/OE/OETIKER/:

CallBackery-0.61.2.tar.gz
  sha256 654458d3badd80c683653dcc1b35fade304779f0668f39127818ce07794f96a7

0.60.0 has no traversal-test finding. The 0.60.0 -> 0.60.1 diff adds both
the validation/open hardening in Doc.pm and the rejection regression test;
it also packages existing tests omitted from the previous MANIFEST.
0.61.2 already contains the same doc-traversal.t bytes as 0.61.3 and also
fires the old suspicious rule. Thus the immediate prior release does not
support a newly introduced attack in 0.61.3.
0.61.2 -> 0.61.3 changes only release metadata/changelog/MANIFEST, the
package version, one AbstractForm.pm assignment, and a new getter test.
The assignment reuses the already computed $value rather than invoking
getFieldValue($key) a second time. No dependencies or frontend bytes change.

Other reviewed behavior
Login sends credentials through the configured same-application JSON-RPC
client and, on success, submits a same-origin hidden /login iframe to offer
password saving. Action.js renders print content into win.document and
appends file fields/session information to FormData for the relative upload
endpoint. HtmlBox deliberately recreates embedded script elements in app
HTML. These behaviors fit the framework and are unchanged from 0.61.2.
Config.pm uses Crypt::Rijndael for encrypted configuration backup/restore,
chmod 0600/0400 for secrets, and sqlite3 for dump/restore. Abstract.pm uses
open3 with a program and argument list; no shell is required by that call.
The installer declares dependencies and exposes an explicit thirdparty make
target using the standard cpanmin.us bootstrap. No concealed payload,
external credential sink, or unrelated executable sidecar was identified.
Source and parser facts were reviewed, including recovered literals; no
obfuscated execution layer was found. This is an artifact judgement;
deployment configuration and third-party dependencies were not supplied.

Trait changes and placement
- Keep the double-colon literal matcher and scope; describe it as a literal
  at notable. HTTP delivery still activates the separate suspicious rule.
  Add the canonical requests.get reference to that rule; its previous GET
  directory selector missed Python requests due to the existing placement.
- Move generic write(content/file) text to source call syntax. It cannot
  establish a filesystem receiver. Preserve its matcher and exclusions.
- Move generic append/get/post method observations to source call syntax;
  FormData.append and server-route registration are decisive counterexamples
  to DOM insertion and LWP-request claims. Preserve matchers and scopes and
  update consumers. The hidden-HOME LWP consumer now also requires the
  existing LWP import evidence, as its name and description require.
- Move open3 call evidence from shell to exec; require a call rather than
  an import/name mention. To retain the existing exec directory budget,
  relocate the existing explicit /bin/sh exec observation to shell/lang,
  preserving its matcher, scope and callers.
- Add a Rijndael constructor and decrypt method observation. Extend the
  canonical encrypt-method observation to Perl and rename/update its Rust
  consumer rather than duplicating the matcher in another language file.

Regression controls
Seven benign fixtures exercise rejection tests, browser printing/FormData,
server-route registration, crypto operations, argv process creation, inert
mentions/imports and near misses. A separate HTTP traversal-request fixture
requires the existing suspicious delivery composite. Expectations are wired
into testdata/expectations.toml. The archive rerun has no hostile or suspicious
traits; the traversal literal and real crypto/process evidence remain notable.
